tests-fixtures.rationale: These writes create synthetic test media or an explicitly development-only captured fixture; neither path is a released runtime authority or delivery.

docs-build-tooling.rationale: These calls materialize schemas, calibration inputs, or retained baseline evidence used to test and document the current system; they are not invoked as released editing authorities.

temp-cache.rationale: Each listed site is confined to a reviewed scratch, response cache, or content-addressed cache lifecycle; promoted media or verdicts are independently re-created or revalidated and do not derive authority from these paths.

governed-production-authority.rationale: Every discovered production-state writer is now bound either to a first-class artifact row or to the explicit legacy governed-state family; this mandatory empty category catches future unbound writers.

delivery-output.rationale: Every discovered editor-facing media/output writer is now bound either to a first-class artifact row or to the explicit legacy delivery family; this mandatory empty category catches future unbound delivery paths.

unknown.rationale: Any site that cannot be assigned safely remains a release blocker; this retained snapshot has no unreviewed file, but the category is mandatory so future drift cannot disappear into a default.

tests-fixtures.rationale: No production-scope child-process boundary in this snapshot exists solely to create a test fixture.

docs-build-tooling.rationale: These child processes measure or generate retained P0 baseline and inventory evidence and are not released editing-path writers.

temp-cache.rationale: These boundaries perform read-only media, font, tool, or liveness probes, or build reconstructable response caches; captured output and cache bytes never grant edit or promotion authority.

governed-production-authority.rationale: All discovered production-state process boundaries now bind to a governed artifact family or a dedicated launcher contract; this mandatory empty category catches future unbound process effects.

delivery-output.rationale: All discovered encoder, Hyperframes, transcript, proxy, and editor-export process boundaries now bind to a delivery artifact family; this mandatory empty category catches future unbound tool outputs.

unknown.rationale: Generic command wrappers, native desktop launchers, Palmier preflight, and FRAME.IO report generation now have explicit input/output and durability contracts; this mandatory empty category fails closed on any future unknown boundary.

knownLimitations: The category is assigned at source-file granularity; a file can contain several primitive calls, all of which inherit the most conservative lifecycle classification for that file.

The AST scan recognizes declared Python and TypeScript filesystem primitives, selected write wrappers, direct child-process calls, and the runCmd/spawnPython TypeScript wrappers, but arbitrary custom-wrapper call graphs require explicit family evidence.

Spawned process inputs and output domains are inventoried by bounded tool/artifact family; per-argument dataflow is not yet proven for every FFmpeg, Hyperframes, Demucs, Codex, or Python child invocation, so family binding is not per-output lineage proof.
External services, databases, and sources outside the declared production-source roots remain outside this repository-local evidence set.
